name: Tree Coloring (Easy Version)
description: This is the Easy version of the problem. The difference between the versions is that in this version, you are only required to find the minimum number of operations. You can hack only if you solved all versions of this problem. You are given a rooted tree$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, where the root has index $$$1$$$, and each vertex is initially white. Define $$$d_i$$$ as the distance from the root to the $$$i$$$-th vertex. You can perform the following operations any number of times: Select a subset $$$S$$$ of white vertices such that no two nodes in $$$S$$$ are connected by an edge, or have the same distance to node $$$1$$$. Formally, $$$S$$$ should satisfy for all $$$x,y\in S$$$ and $$$x\neq y$$$, $$$d_x\neq d_y$$$ and there are no edges between $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$. Color the vertices in $$$S$$$ black. Your job is to find the minimum number of operations required to color the full tree black. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. A rooted tree is a tree where one vertex is special and called the root.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) – the number of vertices in the tree. The $$$i$$$-th following $$$n-1$$$ lines contain two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1\le u_i,v_i\le n$$$, $$$u_i\neq v_i$$$) – the ends of the $$$i$$$-th edge. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2\cdot10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output the minimum number of operations on a new line.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2183D1 — Tree Coloring (Easy Version) [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
